findings.title: x
findings.message: The next() method body is corrupted: it contains the literal text `p.[REDACTED]` instead of a call that advances the scanner (e.g. p.token = p.s.Scan()). The package will not compile, and the token would never advance.

findings.title: Unary operator handling ignores error before negation
findings.message: Unary minus parses its operand with min precedence 3, so no binary operator is consumed. For '-2 mm * 3' it works by luck, but after the unary branch the loop continues and applies binary ops to the negated value, which is fine. However, a.n is negated even when e != nil; harmless since returned value is discarded. More importantly, the Int/Float case: ParseFloat on text like '1e-2' works, but a following identifier 'e' unit handling is fine. Main issue is limited: the unit lookup after a number ignores unknown identifiers (e.g. '2 foo'), leaving the token as Ident so the caller yields a generic error.
findings.suggestion: Check the error before negating, and report unknown unit identifiers explicitly.
